conviction_note: Q3 2026 has not been pre-released (only 9M deliveries), but the bar was reset on the 13 Oct pre-close call, which Jefferies called 'mostly negative' and after which Porsche collected estimates 'only based on the statements of today's call'. The remaining news is a likely trim of the 35-36bn revenue guide and the 24-26% BEV-share guide, which the 21-analyst consensus (34.83bn) already sits below. So the size is a guidance-day size (abs 5.5) and the sign is close to a coin flip (p_up 53). The findings sum (-0.3) and the scaled number (+0.33) differ in sign. Both are near zero, and they come apart because the one positive finding (a consensus the company guided down) moves p_up a little, while the two small negatives are one-off and guidance items the market largely expects.

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue and RoS are new. The consensus was set after the company's 13 Oct pre-close steer (Q3 revenue 8.51bn on 7 estimates, EPS 0.428 on 4). I expect it in line to slightly above on operating profit, with the GTS/Turbo/GT mix offset by Cayenne Electric margin dilution

The revenue guide of 35-36bn is likely trimmed to the low end or below: 9M at consensus is ~25.7bn, so Q4 would need >=9.3bn on -16% volume, and the 21-analyst FY consensus is 34.83bn. The BEV-share guide of 24-26% is likely cut (9M deliveries BEV ~21.7%). The RoS range of 5.5-7.5% is probably held or narrowed. Down on the headline, largely in the bar

Q3 one-offs are unknown: closure charges for Cellforce, eBike Performance and Cetitec, a possible Bugatti Rimac disposal result, and the Manthey step-up. Slight negative on reported EBIT; a gain would be a one-off the market sells
The ANC margin guide was already raised on 9 Sep with the disposal cash. Not expected to move

findings.finding: Porsche's 13 Oct Q3 pre-close call reset the bar down: Jefferies wrote that management's comments were 'overwhelmingly negative' and repeatedly stressed EV margin dilution. Porsche then asked analysts to submit estimates based only on that call. The Q3 consensus is therefore company-steered and low, and the last quarterly statement under the same process (Q1 2026) beat group EBIT consensus by 7%
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 EBIT 7% above consensus (Jefferies, 29 Apr 2026): +1.78% the next session. H1 2026 RoS 7.8%: opened +2.9%, closed -1.47% (beat partly a provision release). Q3 2025 statement (24 Oct 2025, after close): +2.97% the next session
findings.original_quote: Die Äußerungen des Managements des Sportwagenbauers seien überwiegend negativ gewesen, wobei wiederholt auf die Margenverwässerung durch das E-Autogeschäft hingewiesen worden sei (translation: management's comments were predominantly negative, with repeated reference to margin dilution from the EV business)
findings.why_not_priced: The negative steer is priced: the stock fell 2.0% on 13 Oct and is down 7.2% over 20 sessions. What is not priced is the asymmetry it leaves. If the market doubted that the guided consensus could be met, the stock would have fallen further after the 14 Oct estimate deadline. Instead it traded 41.0-43.0 and the register shows no short build. Since this is an inference about how a steered bar resolves, not a number, it is sized small
findings.independence: The Porsche pre-close deck asks for estimates 'only based on the statements of today's call' (https://investorrelations.porsche.com/~/media/Files/P/porsche-ir/results-and-presentations/financial-reports-and-presentation/2026/q3/PCC_Results_Q3.pdf). UBS cut EBIT forecasts for every European carmaker except Porsche AG and Ferrari (https://www.finanzen.ch/analyse/porsche-vz-buy-1110104). Deutsche Bank expects mix to hold revenue up (https://www.finanzen.ch/analyse/porsche-vz-buy-1110881). The Q1 beat is in Jefferies' 29 Apr note (https://live.deutsche-boerse.com/nachrichten/ANALYSE-FLASH-Jefferies-belaesst-Porsche-AG-auf-Hold---Ziel-41-Euro-cc4fa94d-0275-4cf1-9802-45f1feaf567a)

findings.finding: Two FY2026 guidance lines look unreachable on the company's own numbers. Revenue: H1 17.23bn plus Q3 consensus 8.51bn leaves Q4 needing >=9.26bn against 9.41bn in Q4 2025, with volume -16%, and the 21-analyst FY consensus (34.83bn) is already below the 35bn floor. BEV share: 9M deliveries are ~21.7% BEV (Macan Electric 23,029 + Cayenne Electric 7,002 + Taycan 8,699 of 178,532) against a 24-26% guide. A trim on 27 Oct is likely
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 28 Apr 2025 evening forecast cut (ad-hoc 19:31) brought -4.13% the next session after a -6.8% gap. Reaffirmed guides: H1 2026 -1.47%, Q1 2026 +1.78%
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The consensus revenue figure already sits below the guided range, and Deutsche Bank's preview (Oct 13/20) expects a reaffirmation, so a trim to roughly 35bn lands on the bar. The unpriced part is whether the RoS range moves with the revenue range. Sized small and negative, with a wide range, because a guidance change is where European moves have been largest
findings.independence: Consensus 34.83bn FY revenue below the range (https://www.finanzen.ch/nachrichten/aktien/ausblick-porsche-vz-stellt-zahlen-zum-juengsten-quartal-vor-1036664389). H1 guide and the H1 BEV share of 19.4% (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/porsche-ag-achieves-further-milestones-and-stabilises-profitability/d0471b0e-384c-43b5-8c94-45f8ce7d7dbb_en)

findings.finding: At the 7 Oct CMD Porsche announced the planned closure of Cellforce, Porsche eBike Performance and Cetitec's development and production. Charges for this, on top of the Future Package costs the CFO put at a 'three-digit-million amount' for H2, can land in Q3 reported EBIT or in the Q4 guide
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 carried ~EUR 2.7bn of extraordinary expenses, flagged in advance by a Sep 2025 ad-hoc; the release day brought +2.97% the next session, so one-offs the market knows about are looked through
findings.why_not_priced: No amount has been disclosed for these closures, so it cannot be in the consensus number except as a guess. The CFO said the FY guide includes EUR 800-900m of net extraordinary burdens (H1 net ~EUR 100m), so most of this probably sits inside the guide. It is sized as a fraction of its money because it is a one-off with no path to the medium-term targets
